en: Points of Controversy The Great Fifty Second Chapter
The Discourse on the Stability of Consciousness:
Does one consciousness persist for a day? Yes.
Is half a day the moment of arising and half a day the moment of passing away?
One should not say so.
Does a single consciousness persist for two days? One should not say so.
“Yes,” [you say].
“Then is the day the moment of arising, and the day the moment of passing away?
You should not speak thus.
A single consciousness persists for four days … it persists for eight days … it persists for ten days.
It remains for twenty days;
it remains for a month;
it remains for two months.
He remains for four months;
he remains for eight months;
he remains for ten months.
He remains for one year… he remains for two years… he remains for four years…
It remains for eight years … it remains for ten years … it remains for twenty years …
It remains for thirty years...
it remains for forty years...
it remains for fifty years...
It remains for a hundred years...
it remains for two hundred years...
it remains for four hundred years...
It remains for five hundred years...
it remains for one thousand years...
it remains for two thousand years...
It remains for four thousand years...
it remains for eight thousand years...
it remains for sixteen thousand years...
He remains for an eon… he remains for two eons… he remains for four eons…
He remains for eight eons...
he remains for sixteen eons...
he remains for thirty-two eons...
He remains for sixty-four eons… he remains for five hundred eons… he remains for a thousand eons…
It remains for two thousand eons … it remains for four thousand eons … it remains for eight thousand eons …
He remains for sixteen thousand eons … he remains for twenty thousand eons … he remains for forty thousand eons …
"It remains for sixty thousand eons...
it remains for eighty-four thousand eons"?—
Yes, that is so.
Is it the case that the moment of arising lasts for forty-two thousand eons and the moment of passing away lasts for forty-two thousand eons?
One should not say so.
Does a single state of consciousness persist for a day?
“Yes.
“Are there other phenomena that, having arisen for even a single day, cease in abundance?
“Yes.”
Are those phenomena of quick transformation compared to the mind?
One should not say so.
Are those phenomena of quick transformation compared to the mind?
“Yes, [it is so].
“But has it not been said by the Blessed One:
‘Bhikkhus, I do not see even a single other thing that revolves so swiftly as the mind’?”
“Monks, it is not easy to find even a simile for how quickly the mind turns.
Is this indeed a sutta? Yes.
In that case, it should not be said:
"Those phenomena are quick in their revolution compared to consciousness.
Are those phenomena quick in their revolution compared to consciousness?
“Yes, [it is so].
“But was it not said by the Blessed One:
‘Bhikkhus, just as a monkey roaming through a forest or jungle grasps a branch, lets that go and grasps another, lets that go and grasps another;’”
“In the same way, bhikkhus, that which is called ‘mind’ (citta), or ‘intellect’ (mano), or ‘consciousness’ (viññāṇa), arises as one thing and ceases as another, both by night and by day.
Is this indeed a sutta?
Yes, it is.
In that case, it should not be said:
"Those states are quick to change with the mind.
Does one single state of consciousness persist for a whole day?
“Yes,” [you say].
“Does visual consciousness persist for a whole day?
One should not say so.

Accompanied by views … accompanied by doubt … accompanied by sloth …
Does a mind accompanied by restlessness … accompanied by lack of moral shame … accompanied by lack of moral dread persist for a whole day?
It should not be said thus … [as before] … Does one single consciousness last for a day? Yes.
With the very same mind by which one sees a form with the eye, with that same mind one hears a sound with the ear … pe … one smells an odor with the nose … one tastes a flavor with the tongue …

One touches a tangible object with the body … one cognizes a mental phenomenon with the mind …pe… by the very same mind with which one cognizes a mental phenomenon with the mind, by that very same mind one sees a form with the eye …pe…
One hears a sound with the ear...
one smells an odor with the nose...
one tastes a flavor with the tongue... and so forth...
“Does one touch a tangible object with the body?
“One should not say so.
… [as before] … “Does a single consciousness last for a whole day?”
“Yes,” he replied.
“With the very same mind by which one advances, with that same mind one retreats;
with the very same mind by which one retreats, with that same mind one advances.”
With the very same mind by which he looks forward, with that same mind he looks around;
with the very same mind by which he looks around, with that same mind he looks forward;
with the very same mind by which he bends, with that same mind he stretches.
"Does one extend [the arm] with the same mind with which one withdraws it?
"One should not say so...
"...Do the deities who have attained the sphere of infinite space remain with a single mind for as long as their lifespan lasts?"
“Yes.
[The opponent asks: “Is it the case that for human beings, a single state of consciousness persists for the duration of their lifespan?
[The respondent replies: “One should certainly not say so.”
Is it the case that for the gods who have reached the sphere of infinite space, a single state of consciousness persists for the duration of their lifespan?
Yes. [Is it the same] for the gods of the Four Great Kings... [and so on]? Yes.
...of the gods of the Thirty-three,
...of the Yāma gods,
...of the Tusita gods...
...of the gods who delight in creation (Nimmānarati-devas)...
of the gods who wield power over the creations of others (Paranimmitavasavatti-devas)...
of the gods of Brahma’s retinue (Brahmapārisajja-devas)...
...of the gods who are Ministers of Brahmā ...
of the gods who are Great Brahmās ...
of the gods of Limited Radiance ...

...of the Appamāṇasubha devas ...
of the Subhakiṇha devas ...
of the Vehapphala devas ...
...of the Aviha devas...
of the Atappa devas...
of the Sudassa devas...
“Does a single consciousness of the Sudassī devas … of the Akaniṭṭha devas persist for the duration of their lifespan?
One should not say so.

The lifespan of the gods who have reached the base of infinite space is twenty thousand eons; does one single consciousness of those gods who have reached the base of infinite space persist for twenty thousand eons?
Yes. The lifespan of human beings is one hundred years; does one single consciousness of human beings persist for one hundred years?
It should not be said so.

Is it the case that the lifespan of the gods who have reached the sphere of infinite space is twenty thousand eons, and that a single consciousness of those gods who have reached the sphere of infinite space persists for twenty thousand eons?
Yes, it is.

The lifespan of the gods of the Four Great Kings is five hundred years; a single thought-moment of the gods of the Four Great Kings lasts for five hundred years… it lasts for one thousand years… it lasts for two thousand years.
It remains for four thousand years… it remains for eight thousand years… it remains for sixteen thousand years…
He remains for a third part of an aeon … he remains for half an aeon … he remains for one aeon …
He remains for two eons … he remains for four eons … he remains for eight eons …
He remains for sixteen eons...
he remains for thirty-two eons...
he remains for sixty-four eons...
It remains for five hundred eons;
it remains for a thousand eons;
it remains for two thousand eons.

Does it remain for four thousand aeons… does it remain for eight thousand aeons… is the life-span of the Akaniṭṭha devas sixteen thousand aeons, and does a single thought-moment of the Akaniṭṭha devas remain for sixteen thousand aeons?
It should not be said so.
Is it the case that the mind of the devas who have reached the sphere of infinite space arises for a moment and ceases for a moment?
Yes, it is.
Is it not the case that the gods who have reached the sphere of infinite space pass away moment by moment and arise moment by moment?
One should not say so.
Then, does a single consciousness of the gods who have reached the sphere of infinite space persist for the duration of their lifespan?
“Yes,” [you say].
“Then do the gods who have reached the sphere of infinite space pass away with the very same consciousness with which they were reborn?
You should not say so… [and so on]…
The Discussion on the Stability of Consciousness is finished.
